analysis_notes.provenance: Translated English dub of a Chinese animated horror series (stick-figure characters over painted backgrounds; 奠, 车门, 出口 Chinese signage; names Dong/Xiao Wu). Machine translation artifacts: Xiao Wu flips between he/she, 'hook 1574' for plate J1574. Per BRIEF rule 5: study structure only, do not copy story.

title_pattern.notes: No descriptive title; the same 4-hashtag string on every upload from this channel. Discovery is entirely feed-driven: the 'anime' tags target the anime-edit audience while the burned first caption ('cut off a funeral procession') does the title's job. For our channel, a hashtag-only title is a viable test for TikTok but useless for YouTube Shorts search; put the hook in caption 1 instead.

thumbnail.composition: TikTok cover = first frame. 9:16 black canvas; a ~4:3 animation panel centred vertically (roughly y 29-71%); caption line just above the panel. Inside: over-the-shoulder POV from the truck driver's seat, back of a round cartoon head big in the left third, dashboard bottom, through the windshield a black hearse centred-right on a curving night highway with a coin-and-red-tassel charm hanging in the middle.
thumbnail.text: One white italic sans line above the panel: 'cut off a funeral procession' (a fragment of the hook sentence, not a designed headline). The white 奠 funeral character on the hearse glass is the strongest graphic element.
thumbnail.colours: Near-monochrome cold blue-grey night; pure black letterbox; whites (奠 glyph, road lines, round head) and one red accent (tassel, tail lights).
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Huge dark silhouette head foreground vs small hearse in the distance: puts the viewer in the driver's seat, with the threat small, centred and framed by the windshield.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Reads as a story already in motion rather than an ad; the funeral glyph plus hearse plus night road signal horror instantly even without understanding Chinese; the caption fragment begs the question 'what happens if you do?'. Simple flat cartoon character on realistic painted background is a recognisable 'anime story' style in the feed.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: Every trucker knows you never cut off a funeral procession, no matter how slow they're going. People say it's out of respect for the dead, but honestly, everyone's just scared of bad luck.
hook.device: Insider taboo rule ('Every [profession] knows you never [X]') followed by a debunk-turned-fear twist ('respect... but honestly, everyone's scared'). Starts mid-world with no intro; the first frame already shows the hearse. Three cuts in the first 5.5 s (POV, cab exterior, 奠 extreme close-up) plus a 1.7 s first shot.
hook.on_screen: Burned caption fragments synced to the voice; first one 'cut off a funeral procession'.

beats.summary: States a trade taboo ('every trucker knows you never cut off a funeral procession') and its real motive (fear of bad luck) over the hearse POV.
Procession merges in front; vivid inventory of omens: black lead sedan with white flowers and hazards, hearse with funeral character, casket glimpsed through glass.
Passenger asks to pass; narrator refuses: the dead have right of way, you never pass a hearse, 'rule of our trade'.
47 km to next exit; this stretch is cursed and kills a dozen people a year, so following slowly is 'safe'.
Passenger rolls the window down and spits; narrator snaps at him (never open a window at night); passenger goes silent with a strange expression.
A big rig overtakes the procession (plate detail J1574) and stops across its path; convoy halts.
Rig driver walks stiffly, dragging his feet, to the hearse, kowtows three times so hard it thuds, raises his hands as if begging.
Hearse opens; driver tears a strip of the white casket cloth and gives it to him; he drives away.
Narrator explains the local custom of blocking the hearse to receive mourning cloth; tension drops, feels rational.
Convoy resumes; heavy silence; passenger turns away; mat trailing the hearse flickers in headlights.
Passenger says the portrait on the coffin looked like her uncle; narrator dismisses it.
Soft click: seatbelt off, blank face, hand shoots to the door handle.
Door pops open, door-warning light, hard braking and screeching tyres; passenger leaps out, rolls, stands up unhurt and ignores the narrator.
Passenger walks with the same stiff, foot-dragging gait to the hearse, which has stopped as if waiting, and repeats the three kowtows, hands raised.
Hearse window lowers; a thin bony hand offers the white cloth; passenger takes it 'like a devout believer'.
Back in the cab: folds cloth into pocket, hands placed neatly on knees, stares ahead in pale dashboard glow, drained face.
Passenger claims it was a maternal uncle and she had to do the ritual; narrator notes she is an only child and he never knew of maternal siblings.
After 10 minutes the passenger offers to take the wheel; narrator agrees; video cuts off mid-sentence, implying part 2 and a possessed driver.

pacing.note_wpm: Very fast TTS, apparently sped up ~1.5x from normal; one voice for narration and all dialogue; dialogue lines are not tagged, so context does the speaker attribution.
pacing.shot_note: 73 detected cuts in 202 s (~2.8 s); counting punch-ins/inset pops, the picture changes about every 2 s. Hook section is faster (~1.6 s/shot). Long held shots are reserved for the explanation stretch (80-92 s).
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: roughly every 12-20 s a new escalation (new rule, rig overtakes, kowtow, custom explained, uncle twist, seatbelt click, door opens, mirror kowtow, bony hand, cliffhanger)
pacing.caption_style: white italic sans (Arial-like), 1-2 lines, ~5-9 words per card, centred above the panel on black, no highlight/karaoke, changes every ~1.4 s

techniques_worth_copying: Open with a profession-specific rule/taboo stated as common knowledge, then state why people really obey it (fear); 'rules horror' framing primes the viewer to wait for a rule to be broken.
Plant two rules early (never pass a hearse; never roll down the window at night) and show the companion breaking the minor one at 30 s: a silent cause the ending later pays off.

Mirror structure: a stranger performs an uncanny ritual (stiff walk, three kowtows, hands raised), it gets a rational explanation (false relief), then the trusted companion performs the identical ritual. Repetition makes the second time terrifying.
Concrete sensory and numeric details as credibility anchors: 47 km to the exit, a dozen deaths a year, plate J1574, 'thud from dozens of meters away', the soft click of a seatbelt.
Small physical tells for possession: seatbelt slipping off, blank face, hands neatly on knees, staring ahead, pale dashboard light on the face.
Doubt seed in the last 20 s (only child, unknown maternal uncle) undermining the explanation the possessed character gives.
End mid-sentence on an ominous offer (let me drive) for a series cliffhanger; no CTA, no outro, which also drives replays and follows for part 2.
Bookend visuals: the final shot repeats the opening POV of the hearse through the windshield.
Recurring visual motif as punctuation: the 奠 glyph extreme close-up inserted at 4 s, 14 s, 98 s, used as a beat separator.
Insert close-ups for every action verb (brake pedal, screeching tyre, door-warning light, licence plate, bony hand): each sentence gets its own picture.
Dread shading: a black gradient pulled down over the upper face of the flat cartoon character whenever fear rises; cheap and very legible.
Circular inset bubbles for information or flashback (exit sign, sedan memory) instead of cutting away.

Simple flat stick-figure characters (round white heads, dot eyes, expressive brows) composited over moody, realistic painted backgrounds: the contrast is the style and keeps character animation cheap.
Very fast single-voice TTS (~370 wpm) with burned captions: dense storytelling in ~3 min holds attention and suits the read-along TikTok audience.

code_only_remake_needs.canvas: 1080x1920 black canvas with a centred ~4:3 (1080x810) story panel at about 29-71% height; caption zone directly above the panel. Optionally use the full 9:16 for ours, but the letterbox look is part of the 'anime repost' feel.
code_only_remake_needs.characters: SVG rig for flat stick-figure people: round white head with thick black outline, dot eyes, swappable brow/mouth shapes (neutral, angry with red zig-zag marks, shocked O mouth, sad brows), grey nose blush, solid shirt torso (blue/brown), thin stick limbs. Poses: sitting at wheel, turned to window, walking with stiff dragging gait, kneeling, forehead to ground, prone with arms raised, holding a cloth. Dread shading = linear-gradient mask over the upper face.
code_only_remake_needs.backgrounds: Painted-look night scenes as layered SVG/Canvas: truck cab interior from 4 angles (driver POV through windshield, frontal exterior of cab, passenger side window, dashboard), highway with fog (Canvas noise or blurred SVG layers), black sedan and hearse vector illustrations (front and rear), container rig, moonlit sky. Grain/vignette/fog overlay and a cold blue-grey palette with red accents.
code_only_remake_needs.props_inserts: Funeral glyph on rear glass (use our own symbol/text, not a copied frame), flower bow on hood, hanging charm with pendulum swing, licence plate, dashboard gauges with glowing warning icon, brake pedal, tyre with smoke particles, bony hand + white cloth, casket under cloth.
code_only_remake_needs.camera: Per-shot Ken Burns: slow push-ins, punch-in cuts (scale 1.0 to 1.3 on a cut), lateral pans for passing vehicles, small shake on impacts, forward-tracking road lines for windshield POV. Circular inset bubble component (mask + pop-in spring).
code_only_remake_needs.captions: Word-timed captions from TTS timestamps rendered as white italic sans, 1-2 lines of 5-9 words, changing ~every 1.4 s, centred above the panel.
code_only_remake_needs.audio: Kokoro/Piper TTS for a single narrator at ~1.4-1.5x speed (target 330-370 wpm), plus low drone bed, tyre screech, door-alarm chime, thud SFX on kowtows (royalty-free or synthesised).
code_only_remake_needs.storyboard: Shot every ~2-3 s mapped to sentence boundaries, roughly 70-80 shots for 3 min; reuse ~10 background setups with different crops and character poses to keep asset count low (the original reuses the cab and windshield POV constantly).
